name: US recession risk
summary: Sahm recession indicator 0.00 for October; yield curve +0.29 on 23 Nov; jobless claims 203,000
state: The real-time Sahm rule indicator was 0.00 for October, far from the 0.5 trigger (FRED). The 10y–2y Treasury curve was +0.29 on 23 Nov (FRED). Initial jobless claims were 203,000 in the week to 14 Nov, near their one-year low (FRED). No negative GDP quarter is in the latest releases.
for_you: US labour market data show no recession signal. A US downturn would matter for UK exports and global markets.
why: A US recession drags world trade, earnings and jobs; it is the single biggest swing factor for the global cycle.
drivers: Labour market, consumer spending, credit conditions, rates and fiscal policy.

rubric.alert: Sahm ≥ 0.50, or two consecutive negative GDP quarters, or NBER declares recession.
rubric.watch: Sahm 0.30–0.49, or one negative GDP quarter, or payrolls negative in a release.
rubric.normal: Sahm rule indicator < 0.30 and no negative GDP quarter in the latest two releases.
